_comment: Hostname-keyed curated overrides for the enrichment script (travel policy only — application status is time-varying and would rot here). Sources verified 2026-08-16; refresh when an org announces a policy change.

travel.evidence: Curated: HackMIT runs a separate travel-application cycle reimbursing up to ~80% of travel for hackers coming from >50 miles away (was a $200 cap in earlier years).
Curated: TreeHacks covers meals, travel, and lodging for accepted out-of-area hackers ("We take care of meals, travels, and lodging" — treehacks.com).
Curated: PennApps historically provides chartered buses for schools plus direct travel reimbursements (reported up to $500).
Curated: HooHacks has stated "We will provide travel reimbursement" on its 2024-2026 Devpost listings.
Curated: YHack lets accepted participants apply for need-based travel reimbursement, with most support for East-Coast travel.
Curated: Cal Hacks runs a travel-stipend application (apply.calhacks.io/travel); amounts are need-based and not published.
Curated: McHacks FAQ — "we are not able to provide travel reimbursements, however we will have sleeping areas available at the venue itself."
Curated: HackGT (HexLabs) admits through two pools — a travel-reimbursement pool and a non-reimbursement pool; amounts vary by year.
Curated: MHacks has offered travel reimbursement up to $300 USD for accepted hackers.
Curated: Hack@Brown offers travel reimbursement to accepted hackers (standby admits excluded).
Curated: ShellHacks does not offer financial travel reimbursement; it charters coach buses to select Florida schools instead.
Curated: Knight Hacks does not provide travel reimbursement beyond chartered buses (FIU/UF/USF) due to budget constraints.
